source.audit: TutorBench Evaluation Framework / Pedagogy Taxonomy Research Audit

domains.label: Mathematics
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: quantifiers, counterexamples, and distinction between verification and proof
teachingRiskExamples: rewarding a correct final answer despite circular or invalid proof
treating numerical checks as a substitute for general proof

domains.label: Statistics
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: variation, measurement, estimation uncertainty, and model fit
separation of association from causal identification
teachingRiskExamples: formulaically correct work with an invalid interpretation
ignoring selection, sampling, or measurement bias

domains.label: Physics
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: conservation laws, dimensions, approximations, and regime of validity
teachingRiskExamples: reusing a formula after its assumptions no longer hold
treating a model representation as the physical system itself

domains.label: Chemistry
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: coordination of macroscopic observations, microscopic mechanisms, and symbolic representations
conditions, energetics, kinetics, and safety where relevant
teachingRiskExamples: confusing representational convenience with literal particle mechanism
ignoring reaction conditions or conservation constraints

domains.label: Biology
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: multi-level mechanisms involving entities, activities, and organization
evolutionary and functional explanation without teleology
teachingRiskExamples: replacing mechanism with purpose language
treating correlation or a marker as a sufficient disease mechanism

domains.label: Earth / environmental science
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: models, uncertainty, and limits of extrapolation
teachingRiskExamples: inferring climate from a single weather event
generalizing from one location or observation without scope limits

domains.label: Computer science
teachingRiskExamples: assuming one passing test proves general correctness
changing code without evidence that localizes the fault

domains.label: Engineering
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: verification, risk, reliability, and trade-off reasoning
multiple feasible designs under competing objectives
teachingRiskExamples: forcing one unique optimal design without stated objective weights
ignoring manufacturability, safety, cost, or reliability constraints

domains.label: Medicine / health sciences
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: quality of clinical evidence and prior risk
supervision, escalation, uncertainty, and patient safety
teachingRiskExamples: presenting a teaching-case inference as clinical competence
failing to recognize uncertainty or escalation signals

domains.label: Psychology
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: research design, causal identification, reproducibility, and population scope
distinction between group evidence and individual inference
teachingRiskExamples: treating a scale score as the construct itself
using correlational evidence to assert an individual diagnosis

domains.label: Economics
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: separation of empirical claims from normative objectives
teachingRiskExamples: confusing observed price movement with identified causal shock
blending efficiency, distributional values, and empirical estimates

domains.label: Sociology
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: quantitative and qualitative evidence with positionality and scope
teachingRiskExamples: using group averages to stereotype individuals
treating survey, interview, and administrative data as interchangeable evidence

domains.label: Political science / civics
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: distinction between factual and value claims
competing perspectives and public reasoning weighted by evidence
teachingRiskExamples: treating evidence-backed and unsupported claims as equally supported
collapsing policy trade-offs into a single value judgment

domains.label: History
teachingRiskExamples: treating primary-source status as automatic authority
allowing an interpretation that conflicts with the available source evidence

domains.label: Law
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: jurisdiction, controlling authority, and temporal validity
teachingRiskExamples: applying a correct rule from the wrong jurisdiction or date
ignoring authority hierarchy or material factual distinctions

domains.label: Philosophy
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: objections, replies, and distinction among defensible positions
teachingRiskExamples: rewarding agreement with the rubric author's position
treating disagreement as error when multiple arguments are defensible

domains.label: Languages / second-language learning
teachingRiskExamples: treating one native-speaker form as the only valid expression
penalizing variation that does not impair the communicative target

domains.label: Literature
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: historical and genre context with internally coherent interpretation
teachingRiskExamples: forcing one interpretation despite multiple text-supported readings
treating interpretive plurality as permission for evidence-free claims

domains.label: Writing / rhetoric
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: argument, evidence, genre, and revision process
teachingRiskExamples: equating a polished product with demonstrated learner mastery
rewriting the learner's voice without a task-specific reason

domains.label: Business / finance / accounting
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: data quality and accounting or regulatory context
assumptions, decision objectives, risk, and time applicability
separation of rule application from business judgment
teachingRiskExamples: using one profitability metric as a complete decision criterion
ignoring regulatory, risk, or timing constraints

domains.label: Arts / music / design
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: technique, form, expressive intent, and context
teachingRiskExamples: substituting generic aesthetic preference for task evidence
judging process skills only from a textual description of performance

domains.label: Vocational / procedural education
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: tool conditions, quality standards, and safety stops
teachingRiskExamples: treating verbal recall of a procedure as safe execution competence
ignoring stop/recovery conditions in procedural guidance

domains.label: Interdisciplinary / emerging fields
evidenceAndReasoningNorms: compatibility of assumptions and evidence across contributing fields
boundary objects, uncertainty, and scope transfer
explicit handling of stakeholder or objective conflicts
teachingRiskExamples: assuming evidence valid in one field automatically supports another field's conclusion
hiding cross-domain uncertainty behind a single blended answer
